resources.string: LEAKCAM Setup
Connect your LEAKCAM to Wi-Fi in four steps. The phone talks to it over Bluetooth, so stay within a few metres of it.
1. Plug the LEAKCAM into USB power
2. Find it
3. Enter your Wi-Fi network
4. Pair and save
Find LEAKCAM
Wi-Fi name (SSID)
Wi-Fi password
Show password
Pair and save

Plug the LEAKCAM into a USB charger or a computer with its USB-C cable. It can be set up only while it is on USB power: being able to plug it in proves it is yours, so nobody outside your home can pair with it. Then tap Find LEAKCAM.
Looking for LEAKCAM boards nearby…
No LEAKCAM found. Check that it is plugged into USB power and within a few metres, then tap Find LEAKCAM again.
No LEAKCAM found. Check that it is plugged into USB power and within a few metres, and that Location is on (this Android version needs it for Bluetooth scanning), then tap Find LEAKCAM again.
Pick your LEAKCAM (the one with the strongest signal is usually the nearest), then enter the Wi-Fi network it should use.

Enter the name and password of the Wi-Fi network the LEAKCAM should use. It must be a 2.4 GHz network: the LEAKCAM does not see 5 GHz. If your router shows separate names for the two bands, pick the 2.4 GHz one. Leave the password empty for an open network. Then tap Pair and save.
Connecting to %1$s…

Your phone now asks to pair with %1$s.

• Tap Pair (on some phones: Allow or OK).
• There is no PIN to type: the LEAKCAM has no screen or buttons.
• If no request appears, pull down the notification shade and tap the Bluetooth pairing notification.

Pairing is needed only once. It keeps the Wi-Fi password encrypted on its way to the LEAKCAM.
%1$s is already paired with this phone. Sending the Wi-Fi settings…
Paired. Sending the Wi-Fi settings…

Done. %1$s stored the Wi-Fi network \"%2$s\".\n\nYou can unplug it now. It connects to Wi-Fi at its next scheduled check. If it never reports, the name or password was wrong: plug it in again and repeat.
This phone has no Bluetooth, which the setup needs.
Allow Bluetooth access (Nearby devices) so the app can find the LEAKCAM, then tap again.
Bluetooth access allowed. Tap again to continue.
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on, then tap again.
Scanning failed (error %1$d). Turn Bluetooth off and on, then tap Find LEAKCAM again.
Tap Find LEAKCAM and pick your board first.
The Wi-Fi name must be 1 to 32 characters long.
The Wi-Fi password must be 8 to 63 characters long, or empty for an open network.
The LEAKCAM did not answer. Check it is still plugged into USB power and nearby, then try again. If a pairing request is still open on the phone, accept it first.
The LEAKCAM disconnected (status %1$d). Keep it on USB power and nearby, then try again.

Pairing did not go through.

• Was the request declined, or did it time out? Try again and tap Pair.
• Is the LEAKCAM on USB power? It refuses pairing on battery.
The LEAKCAM no longer recognises this phone (it was reset, or paired again elsewhere).\n\nOpen the phone\'s Bluetooth settings, tap %1$s, choose Forget (or Unpair), then tap Pair and save again.
This device is not a LEAKCAM in setup mode. Keep it on USB power and scan again.
The LEAKCAM refused the %1$s (error %2$d). Check it and try again.
Could not send the %1$s. Try again.
